sources.entry: Twipped/InterviewThis: questions to ask prospective employers

summary.one_liner: A large, categorized list of questions developers can ask prospective employers during the hiring process, meant as a reference rather than a script to send wholesale.
summary.what_it_does: The README is an open-ended list of interview questions for software developers to ask potential employers, grouped under headings such as The Position, Team Interactions, Development Process, Monitoring/On-call, Remote, Open Source, Codebase/Architecture, Diversity, Culture, Company, and language-specific sections for PHP and JavaScript plus a System and Network Administration section. Questions are written as bullets with indented follow-ups. The author states it is a reference point to choose from, not a checklist, and says the questions are not all suited to a first interview. The README also invites pull requests and issues with new or reworded questions. It contains no software, only text.
use_cases: Preparing questions to ask at a job interview
Evaluating a prospective employer's engineering culture
Checking a company's remote work and on-call policies before accepting an offer
Comparing development process and tooling at different companies
Contributing new interview questions to a shared list
notable: Organized into topic sections covering position, team, process, remote work, culture, company and system administration
Includes follow-up sub-questions beneath many main questions
Explicitly framed as a selection reference, not a list to send to an employer
Some sections are specific to PHP, JavaScript, and sysadmin tooling
caveats: The author notes many questions are not appropriate for an initial interview and some may be unanswerable by HR screeners
Some sections are tied to specific technologies (PHP, JavaScript, Puppet/Chef) and may not apply to every role
Pull requests may be reworded or rejected by the maintainer
